question_text: According to the course material, BUS207 Business Communication is a two-credit course to be taken in:
option_a: the second year of the undergraduate programme in the Faculty of Management Sciences
explanation: The blurb states BUS207 is a 2-credit course in the second year of the undergraduate programme in the Faculty of Management Sciences.

question_text: According to the course material, communication is a process of transferring information from one entity to another and is commonly defined as the imparting or interchange of thoughts, opinions, or information by speech, writing, or:
explanation: Communication is commonly defined as the imparting or interchange of thoughts, opinions, or information by speech, writing, or signs.

question_text: According to the course material, communication is a process whereby information is enclosed in a package and imparted by a sender to a receiver via a channel or medium; the receiver then decodes the message and gives the sender:
explanation: The receiver decodes the message and gives the sender a feedback.

question_text: According to the course material, two common barriers to successful communication are message complexity and:
option_a: message overload (when a person receives too many messages at the same time)
option_b: only the colour of the shop
explanation: Two common barriers: message overload and message complexity.

question_text: According to the course material, the communication process consists of the sender, encoding, the channel, decoding, the receiver, feedback and:
explanation: Process: sender, encoding, the channel, decoding, the receiver, feedback and the context.

question_text: According to the course material, verbal channels include face-to-face meetings, telephone and videoconferencing, while written channels include letters, emails, memos and:
explanation: Written channels: letters, emails, memos and reports.

question_text: According to the course material, it is not particularly effective to give a long list of directions verbally, while you will quickly cause problems if you give someone negative feedback using:
explanation: A long list of directions is poorly suited to speech; negative feedback by email quickly causes problems.

question_text: According to the course material, communication can be seen as processes of information transmission governed by three levels of semiotic rules: syntactic, pragmatic and:
explanation: Three levels: syntactic (formal properties of signs), pragmatic (signs and users), semantic (signs and what they represent).

question_text: According to the course material, there are three major parts in human face-to-face communication: body language, voice tonality, and words; according to the research, 55% of impact is determined by body language, 38% by tone of voice, and 7% by:
option_a: the content or the words used
explanation: 55% body language, 38% tone of voice, 7% content or words.

question_text: According to the course material, three forms of communication are verbal communication, non-verbal communication and:
explanation: Three forms: verbal, non-verbal, visual.

question_text: According to the course material, Max Weinreich is credited as saying that a language is a dialect with:
explanation: Weinreich: a language is a dialect with an army and a navy.

question_text: According to the course material, poor or inaccurate communication in a globalised environment can lead to conflict and negativity in the workplace and could even lead to cancellation of a deal or:
explanation: Poor communication can cancel a deal or lose customer goodwill.

question_text: According to the course material, communication studies is an academic field commonly defined as the sharing of symbols over distances in:
explanation: Communication studies: sharing of symbols over distances in space and time.

question_text: According to the course material, business communication is the process of exchanging messages or information between two or more parties for the purpose of:
explanation: Business communication exchanges messages to promote business growth.

question_text: According to the course material, at its most basic level the purpose of communication in the workplace is to provide employees with:
option_a: the information they need to do their jobs
explanation: Workplace communication at its most basic provides employees the information they need to do their jobs.

question_text: According to the course material, in organisations communication skill is used to send messages:
explanation: In organisations, communication skill is used to send messages 64% of the time.

question_text: According to the course material, vertical business communication is the form of communication between:
option_a: a worker and his or her boss
option_b: only two customers in a market
option_c: only a doctor and an accident patient
option_d: only a finder of a GSM handset
explanation: Vertical: worker and boss; seniority and chain of command.

question_text: According to the course material, the communication process among workers of the same level is called:
explanation: Horizontal: among workers of the same level; no sense of seniority.

question_text: According to the course material, when workers talk to each other and relay information on to other workers it is called the grapevine, which is:
option_a: the unofficial way that communication takes place in an organization
explanation: The grapevine is unofficial, neither authorised nor supported by the organization.

question_text: According to the course material, quasi-vertical business communication has an intermediary between the communicators, for example communication between management and workers achieved through:
option_a: the labour union which the workers belong to
explanation: Quasi-vertical: e.g. management and workers through the labour union, to emphasise status and independence.

question_text: According to the course material, face-to-face meetings are personal and should be succeeded by:
explanation: Face-to-face meetings should be succeeded by a written follow-up.

question_text: According to the course material, non-verbal communication is a primitive form that does not involve the use of words; it uses gestures, cues, vocal qualities, spatial relationships etc. and is commonly used to express emotions like respect, love and:
explanation: Non-verbal communication commonly expresses emotions like respect, love, dislike.

question_text: According to the course material, good communication is a pre-requisite for:
explanation: Good communication skills boost confidence and clarity; good communication is a pre-requisite for good managers.

question_text: According to the course material, communication requires that all parties have an area of communicative commonality; there are auditory means such as speaking and singing, and nonverbal physical means such as body language, sign language, paralanguage, touch, eye contact, by using:
explanation: Auditory and nonverbal means, including writing.

question_text: According to the course material, a particular instance of communication is called a speech act, and in the presence of communication noise on the transmission channel, reception and decoding of content may be:
explanation: Communication noise can make reception and decoding faulty so the speech act may not achieve the desired effect.
